significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that a trait-carrying reward model can install its trait through a "single trait-free scalar" without teacher tokens, with transmission weaker than SFT, coupled to the "same early-layer trait direction," and gated by reward-model–policy base match; this combines a form-(ii) causal claim with form-(iii) ordering and predictive-coupling claims. Cloud et al.'s Subliminal Learning work makes gradient alignment and shared base models central to the current explanation, so this conclusion would constrain whether that explanation applies to optimization on self-generated outputs and would predict matched-versus-mismatched and RL-versus-SFT outcomes for further traits and carriers. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic account; an H1 null would rule out scalar reward as sufficient under this construction, while separate H2/H3 failures would reject the shared-direction or relocated-gate explanations, though they would not prove that all reward shaping is safe. The branches are determinate, and the topic-substitution check passes: replacing these specific channel, ordering, and gate assertions with merely "extend subliminal learning" would not support this score.

reach.justification: The clearest named handle is the ex-ante design rule to "audit reward-model provenance and matched-base status"; the claim also hands researchers an "early-layer trait steering direction" as a diagnostic and intervention target. Provenance and base-match checks act before RL training or deployment and could therefore change decisions by teams that procure, reuse, audit, or ship reward models, rather than serving only as post-hoc explanation. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive claims still predict the ordering "T_RL < SFT-T," the matched-over-mismatched gate, and alignment with the SFT trait direction, so more than a mere search procedure survives recalibration. Its scope is nevertheless limited to reward models induced from trait-carrying matched-base teachers and does not automatically cover ordinary independently trained reward models; the topic-substitution check passes because subliminal learning alone supplies neither this ex-ante audit rule nor these transferable relations.
